proof.text: Choose K-flat representatives $A,B$ of $K,L$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a K-injective representative $I$ of $M$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Write $\mathscr H$ for the ordinary sheaf Hom complex. The existing chain-level currying isomorphism [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] is $\mathscr H(A,\mathscr H(B,I))\cong\mathscr H(\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes B),I)$, natural in all three complex maps. Its left inner Hom is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective]. Thus the left side computes $H(K,H(L,M))$ and the right side computes $H(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L,M)$: both tensor factors were chosen K-flat, exactly as in the statement's definition of derived tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The representative comparisons and invariance under quasi-isomorphisms [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] descend this natural chain isomorphism to the required natural isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O)$. In Lean, use the existing concrete functorial flat resolution to show that the inclusion of the specified K-flat full subcategory followed by Q is a localization. Replace the third variable functorially by K-injectives. The existing representative comparison computes the inner Hom; quasi-isomorphism invariance computes the outer Hom because the inner Hom is K-injective. Assemble the chain currying comparison and the given tensor comparison on the product of two K-flat subcategories and all complexes. The tensor bifunctor applies its two maps successively; the total-complex map composition lemma identifies this with the simultaneous tensor map in the currying naturality equation. Fully faithful precomposition with the product localization then descends the natural isomorphism in all three variables at once.

Let $A$ represent $L$ and let $I$ be K-injective representing $M$. The six restriction instances proved in this module show directly that slice restriction is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits, so it preserves these representatives and their quasi-isomorphisms. For limits, forget to presheaves of abelian groups, where restriction is precomposition, and reflect limits back. For colimits, the slice functors are both continuous and cocontinuous; their pushforward on abelian sheaves is therefore also a left adjoint. The exact conservative forgetful functor from module sheaves to abelian sheaves reflects the finite colimits. Over $V\to U$, sections of $\mathscr H(A,I)|_U$ and of $\mathscr H(A|_U,I|_U)$ are the same families $A^p|_V\to I^{p+n}|_V$, with the same differential $d_I f-(-1)^n f d_A$ [def-pur-hom-complex, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. This gives a chain isomorphism, and $I|_U$ is K-injective [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized]. Therefore the two sides compute the two derived Homs in the statement [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For $W\to U$, the composite comparison and the direct comparison agree on every such family over each $V\to W$; this proves compatibility with successive slice restrictions. Componentwise pre- and postcomposition commute with these identity maps, proving naturality.

We will use cones of K-injective representatives. If $g:J\to I$ is a chain map with $J,I$ K-injective, then in the homotopy-category cone triangle $J\to I\to C(g)\to J[1]$ [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] to the rotated triangle and an acyclic complex $E$. The map $E\to J[1]$ obtained from any $E\to C(g)$ is zero, since $J[1]$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Exactness factors $E\to C(g)$ through $I$, and that factor is zero for the same reason. Hence $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(E,C(g))=0$, which is exactly K-injectivity of $C(g)$. This is the two-line representable-exactness argument of Stacks Tag 090X (lemma-triangle-K-injective), with all of its inputs already cited.

For the first variable fix a K-injective $I$ representing $M$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By the cone description of distinguished triangles [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], it suffices to start with $A\xrightarrow{f}B\to C(f)\to A[1]$. Put $X=\mathscr H(B,I)$, $Y=\mathscr H(A,I)$, and $h=f^*:X\to Y$. The graded splitting $C(f)=B\oplus A[1]$ writes a degree-$n$ element of $\mathscr H(C(f),I)$ as $(x,y)$ with $x\in X^n$, $y\in Y^{n-1}$. Substitution into the Hom differential [def-pur-hom-complex] gives $d(x,y)=(d_Xx,d_Yy+(-1)^{n+1}h(x))$. The invertible degreewise map $(x,y)\mapsto((-1)^{n-1}y,x)$ identifies this with $C(h)[-1]$, whose differential is $(u,x)\mapsto(-d_Yu-h(x),d_Xx)$. Its projection to $X$ is $x$, and the following map $X\to Y$ is $h$, so the resulting triangle is the inverse rotation of the cone triangle of $h$. Its degree-$n$ boundary $Y\to\mathscr H(C(f),I)[1]$ is $y\mapsto(0,(-1)^n y)$: precomposition with the original boundary $-p:C(f)\to A[1]$ gives exactly this map after the source-shift comparison, whose degree-$r$ component is multiplication by $(-1)^r$ on $Y^{r-1}$. Cone triangles, their rotations and their localized images are distinguished [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated, def-weil-triangulated-category]. Each Hom into $I$ computes derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; hence this is the required reversed triangle. This calculation uses a finite biproduct, with no exactness assumption on infinite products.

source.place: Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated), first-variable termwise split cone calculation

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle in the second variable, choose K-injective representatives $J,I$ of its first two vertices [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Its first morphism lifts to a chain map $g:J\to I$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. The localized cone triangle of $g$ and the given triangle complete the same first arrow; TR3 [def-weil-triangulated-category] gives a triangle morphism with identity first two components, and [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the third an isomorphism. The preceding step about K-injective cones shows that $C(g)$ is K-injective. For any complex $A$ representing the fixed first variable, [lem-sc-hom-complex-mapping-cone] gives $\mathscr H(A,C(g))\cong C(\mathscr H(A,g))$. Under the standard finite-biproduct splitting the differential is $(x,y)\mapsto(d x+\mathscr H(A,g)y,-d y)$ [def-pur-hom-complex], so the inclusion, projection and signed target-shift boundary give the ordinary cone triangle. After localization it is distinguished [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. All three targets are K-injective, so these Homs compute the derived Homs and their arrows [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. This proves the covariant triangle assertion, and the triangle isomorphism just constructed transfers it to the given triangle.

source.place: Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated), second-variable termwise split cone calculation

proof.text: The natural shift comparisons [lem-pur-derived-internal-hom-shift-left, lem-pur-derived-internal-hom-shift-right] are $H(P[m],Q)\cong H(P,Q)[-m]$ and $H(P,Q[n])\cong H(P,Q)[n]$. They supply the source and target shift identifications used in the two cone triangles above. Their differentials are the signed differentials of [def-pur-hom-complex]. Neither comparison requires boundedness, flatness or finite generation; neither did any of the preceding arguments.

For the independent-universe normalized shifts, construct both chain reindexings directly from the fixed Hom product projections [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections, def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. The target reindexing is unsigned; the source reindexing multiplies degree k by (-1)^(s*k). Projection extensionality proves their chain identities, naturality, inverse identities, and the target shift zero/addition coherence. The ordinary-to-derived comparison is the fixed augmentation followed by the inverse localization factorization. Hom into K-injective complexes preserves quasi-isomorphisms [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined-universes], so that comparison is invertible on the K-injective subcategory. The inclusion of this subcategory followed by Q is a localization and an equivalence, by the existing Mathlib K-injective derivability structure. Descend target shift isomorphisms and their coherence through these localizations and then in the source variable. Descend the signed source shift in both variables through product localization. Naturality of the augmentation gives the exact normalization equations. Projection extensionality and essential surjectivity give uniqueness. For covariant exactness, construct Hom(L, cone(f)) as the cone of Hom(L,f) by the two finite-biproduct projections, verifying the differential and all three triangle arrows, including the target-shift boundary. Mathlib right-orthogonal closure shows the cone of a map between K-injectives is K-injective. Lift the first arrow of a distinguished triangle to that full subcategory; TR3 and the two-out-of-three isomorphism theorem identify its cone triangle with the given triangle. Transfer the ordinary cone comparison through the normalized augmentation, giving triangulatedness for the unique normalized target shift. These arguments allow separate object and morphism universes and use neither boundedness nor K-flatness. The local normalization predicates name homComplexπ directly, the same fixed projection as the coefficient projection from homComplex_exists. Specialize the abstract arguments directly to the native Hom functor, projections, and their law lemmas; no concrete proof-bearing data wrapper is unfolded.

title: Derived internal Hom calculus on small ringed sites
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$. Use $D(\mathcal O)$ for the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $H(L,M)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Derived tensor is total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] after K-flat replacement [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For all $K,L,M\in D(\mathcal O)$ there is a natural isomorphism $H(K,H(L,M))\cong H(K\otimes_{\mathcal O}^{\mathbf L}L,M)$. For every object $U$, write $\mathcal O_U$ for restriction to the slice site $\mathcal C/U$. There is a natural isomorphism $H(L,M)|_U\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(L|_U,M|_U)$, compatible with successive slice restrictions. The functor $H$ sends distinguished triangles in either variable to distinguished triangles (contravariantly in the first variable), and commutes with shifts with the corresponding sign of the shift. No boundedness or finite-generation condition is imposed on the three objects.
